outcomes.statement: Compares how Belgium accommodated its linguistic diversity with how majoritarianism in Sri Lanka alienated the Tamils.
Describes the elements of the Belgian model of power sharing, including the community government and equal representation in Brussels.

topics.title: Why and how power is shared

outcomes.statement: Explains the prudential and moral reasons for sharing power.
Classifies forms of power sharing as among organs of government, among levels of government, among social groups, or among parties and pressure groups.

concepts.name: Power sharing in Belgium and Sri Lanka

topics.title: What makes India a federal country

outcomes.statement: Explains what federalism is, and distinguishes 'coming together' from 'holding together' federations.
Describes the three lists that divide power in India, and the special provisions for some States such as Article 371.
Explains how linguistic States, the language policy and centre-state relations have strengthened federalism in India.
Describes decentralisation and the 1992 amendment that created panchayats and municipalities.
Explains the sexual division of labour and why women remain under-represented in politics.
Describes measures for women's representation, including the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam of 2023.
Explains when religion in politics becomes communalism, and how the Constitution makes India secular.
Explains how caste shapes politics, and how politics in turn changes caste.

concepts.name: Communalism, secularism and caste in politics

outcomes.statement: Explains what a political party is and the functions it performs in a democracy.
Compares one-party, two-party and multiparty systems, including the trade-offs of a multiparty system.

topics.title: Parties in India and their challenges

outcomes.statement: Describes what a party must achieve to be recognised as a national or a state party, with examples of India's parties.
Explains the challenges political parties face and the ways they can be reformed.

concepts.name: Meaning and functions of political parties
National and state parties and their challenges

outcomes.statement: Evaluates democracy as accountable, responsive and legitimate government.
Evaluates the economic outcomes of democracy, including growth and the reduction of inequality and poverty.
Explains how democracy accommodates social diversity and upholds the dignity and freedom of citizens.

prerequisites.concept: National and state parties and their challenges
prerequisites.requires: Meaning and functions of political parties
